chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Nufali, on the authority of al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Hoarding (al-hikrah) applies to six items: wheat, barley, dates, raisins, ghee (cooking fat), and oil.

key_terms.التَّمْرُ: Dates, a key fruit and food source.
key_terms.الزَّيْتُ: Oil, typically olive oil in this context.
key_terms.السَّمْنُ: Ghee or clarified butter, used as cooking fat.
key_terms.الْحِكْرَةُ: Hoarding or stockpiling, specifically referring to the act of withholding essential goods from the market to raise prices or for profit.

ai.seo_question: What are the six items subject to hoarding (hikrah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* establishes the foundational categories for *hikrah* (hoarding) in Shia fiqh, limiting the prohibition to six essential, storable food staples: wheat, barley, dates, raisins, ghee, and oil. By specifying these items, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) highlights the economic importance of preserving basic sustenance against market manipulation, a concept that underpins the jurisprudence of *ihtikar*. This enumeration serves as a primary textual basis for distinguishing between permissible storage and exploitative hoarding in Islamic economic law.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-22 Hamzih ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad , on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “
Hoarding (which is bad) implies hoarding any of six items: wheat; barley; dates; raisins; cooking fat and oil.”
